pairs.question: Tu ergo quam consuetudinem sequeris?
pairs.answer: Eadem omnibus pono; ad cenam enim, non ad notam invito cunctisque rebus exaequo, quos mensa et toro aequavi.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange at a dinner. Dropped the speech tag 'inquit' from inside the question. The host's neighbour asks Pliny what custom he follows after Pliny disapproved of the graded wine; Pliny answers. Answer runs to the first full stop (the only sentence-terminator in the reply, semicolons being interior); it is the whole direct reply before the next speaker's 'Etiamne libertos?'.

pairs.question: Etiamne libertos?
pairs.answer: Etiam; convictores enim tunc, non libertos puto.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech follow-up: the interlocutor asks whether Pliny equalises even his freedmen, Pliny answers 'Etiam...'. Answer is the complete reply to its single full stop, before 'Et ille: Magno tibi constat.'

pairs.question: Qui fieri potest?
pairs.answer: Quia scilicet liberti mei non idem quod ego bibunt, sed idem ego quod liberti.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech: after the interlocutor's statement 'Magno tibi constat' and Pliny's retort 'Minime' (a statement/retort, not a Q&A, so excluded), the interlocutor asks how it can be so; Pliny explains. Answer is the full reply to its closing full stop, after which the narration resumes with 'Et hercule si gulae temperes...'. The intervening 'Magno tibi constat'/'Minime' exchange is omitted as not interrogative.
